items.title: Russell takes Baku pole as Antonelli crashes out in Q1
items.summary: George Russell set a 1:42.526 for pole, 0.837s ahead of Charles Leclerc; Oscar Piastri was third, just 0.001s behind Leclerc. Championship leader Kimi Antonelli hit the Turn 1 wall in Q1 and was classified 16th. The official starting grid is now published separately from the qualifying classification.
items.why_it_matters: Mercedes has one car on pole and its other driver starting 16th after a major qualifying incident. Antonelli arrived 81 points ahead of Russell; qualifying itself does not award those championship points.

items.title: FIA confirms five-place Sainz drop and three-place Perez penalty
items.summary: Document 49 gives Carlos Sainz a five-place grid penalty and two penalty points after finding that he failed to slow sufficiently under the single yellow in Marshalling Sector 4; this is separate from his FP3 reprimand. Document 48 gives Sergio Perez a three-place penalty for impeding Oscar Piastri. Formula1.com's published starting grid lists Sainz 14th and Perez 20th, with Alonso 21st and Stroll 22nd after their separate power-unit penalties.
items.why_it_matters: The penalties change the order for Saturday and distinguish two different Sainz yellow-flag incidents. The official starting-grid table, rather than a hand-calculated permutation, is the published reference.

items.title: Gasly leads Alpine's double Q3 appearance in Baku
items.summary: Pierre Gasly qualified seventh and Franco Colapinto tenth, putting both Alpines into Q3. Gasly said interruptions from incidents ahead compromised his final two runs and that he believed more pace was available; Colapinto locked up at Turn 15 on his final-segment lap.
items.why_it_matters: Both cars start inside the top ten on the published grid, giving Alpine a concrete points opportunity; Gasly's comments describe lost qualifying chances, not a guaranteed race result.
